svg.title: One audit row, its eleven columns grouped by the source of each value
svg.desc: The eleven columns of the mcp_audit_log table, grouped under the five places their values come from rather than listed as rows. Under a green heading reading database are four fields: the identifier assigned on insert, the timestamp from the database default now rather than the server clock, the affected row count taken from the last field of PostgreSQL's command tag, and the error message in PostgreSQL's own words on the failure path. Under a terracotta heading reading parse tree are three: the operation, taken from the root node type and not from a keyword match, the target table taken from the Table node, and the statement text, regenerated from the tree with comments stripped. The statement is boxed and an arrow runs from it to the panel below. Under a blue heading reading the human is one field, the note typed by the person who approved the write. Under a grey heading reading the server is one field, the success flag, which is the server's own control flow. Under a plain heading reading environment are two, the session identifier and the actor, both read from the operator environment. The panel below states that the model authored the semantics of exactly one field, the statement text, and that a person read that exact string before it ran. A closing line records that the table is written by the writer role, read through the read-only role, and never exposed as a tool the model can edit.
svg.text: One audit row, and where each value came from
Eleven columns, grouped by source. The model authored the semantics of exactly one of them.
INSERT INTO mcp_audit_log (...) VALUES ($1 ... $9) RETURNING id
id and occurred_at have defaults, so nine values are bound
the root node type, not a
The model authored the semantics of exactly one field, sql_text, and a person read that exact string before it ran.
Every other column comes from the parse tree, the database, the approving human, or the operator's environment.
The table is written by mcp_writer. It is read through the read-only role, and it is not exposed as a tool the model can edit.
